properties.description:

The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S.
Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center.

BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING

IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED

05:30 PST Thu Nov 19 2026

The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY
AVALANCHE WARNING for the following areas: NWS Reno NV - NVZ002
(Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA))

* WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger exists in the backcountry. Large
avalanches are expected across backcountry terrain.

* WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy 49)
on the north and Ebbetts Pass (Hwy 4) on the south, including the
greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to backcountry areas,
not to ski areas and highways where avalanche mitigation programs
exist.

* WHEN...In effect from Thu 05:30 PST to Fri 04:00 PST.

* IMPACTS...Significant amounts of new snow and wind are creating
dangerous avalanche conditions in the backcountry. The new snow is
overloading a weak snowpack in some upper elevation areas.
Avalanches could run down into treed terrain.

* PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche
conditions exist in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below
backcountry avalanche terrain is not recommended during HIGH
avalanche danger.

Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or www.avalanche.org
for more detailed information.

Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage
area of this or any avalanche center.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 19 at 4:41AM PST until November 19 at 10:45AM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Placer County in central California...
Sacramento County in central California...
Northwestern San Joaquin County in central California...
Solano County in central California...
Southern Sutter County in central California...
Yolo County in central California...

* WHEN...Until 1045 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 437 AM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain. This  will cause urban and small stream
flooding. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen in the
last 24 hours, with 0.1 to 0.3 inches in the last hour.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.7 to 1 inch are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sacramento, Stockton, Elk Grove, Roseville, Vallejo,
Fairfield, Vacaville, Citrus Heights, Folsom, Davis, Rocklin,
Woodland, Benicia, Galt, Carmichael, Fair Oaks, Rancho
Cordova, Lodi, West Sacramento and Lincoln.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 1045 AM PST THIS MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Santa Lucia Mountains and Los Padres National Forest; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued November 18 at 9:58PM PST until November 19 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
Between 3 to 6 inches of rain have fallen across the Santa Lucia
Range impacting the Timber and Plaskett Fire Burn Scars over the last
24 hours. Expect additional rounds of scattered moderate to heavy
rain impacting the Central Coast and Napa County through Thursday
evening.

* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Plaskett burn area and Timber burn
area.

* WHERE...For the Timber Scar, portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los
Padres National Forecast from Andrew Molera State Park to
Partington Ridge including the town of Big Sur.

For the Plaskett Scar, areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile
marker 11 including Los Burros Road.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas is
expected during the watch period. Residents near the Timber burn
area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the
drainages within Lafler, Castro, and Graves Canyons, as well as
drainages between Grimes and Castro Canyons.

Residents near the Plaskett burn area should prepare for potential
debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and Prewitt Creeks.

Be sure to stay up to date with information from local authorities.
Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas,
roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas, which may lead
to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Big Sur, Plaskett, and Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
